title: The Perfect Letter
premise: Juniper Villalobos, coroner of the fading town of Marrow Creek, receives a retainer from a stranger named Elias Wren to investigate a murder that hasn't happened yet — his own. Following cryptic entries in an old funeral ledger hidden in her own filing system, Juniper discovers a decades-old conspiracy among the town's founding families to bury a string of deaths as accidents, and that Wren is the son of one of its victims planning to expose it before he becomes its final casualty. As Juniper falls for Wren and realizes her beloved mentor, former coroner Ada Quill, helped forge the records, she must choose between protecting the town's fragile peace and delivering justice the law abandoned. In the end, Juniper publicly reads the ledger at the town's centennial gathering, Ada confesses and turns state's evidence, and Juniper — having saved Wren from the staged 'accident' meant to silence him — finally lets herself belong to someone instead of only to the dead.
about_author: Ines Thornbury is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper obituary writer who spent years listening to what families didn't say about their dead. She lives in a converted funeral parlor in rural New England, where she writes mysteries about quiet places keeping loud secrets.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. A nervous stranger, Elias Wren, walks into the coroner's office and pays a hefty retainer to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — his own. Juniper, who trusts paperwork over people, is unsettled by how much cash he carries and how well he knows her office. Emotional beat: wary curiosity; the first crack in twelve years of routine.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Establishing Marrow Creek's rhythms: Juniper tends the cemetery, greets headstones like old friends, and deflects the sheriff's flirtation. Elias lingers, asking oddly specific questions about deaths from 1989. Emotional beat: loneliness revealed — Juniper knows every grave by name but no living person by heart.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. While re-filing cold case boxes, Juniper notices anomalies in the old funeral ledger: dates out of sequence, initials repeated, cause-of-death codes that don't exist. The ledger was catalogued by her mentor, Ada Quill. Emotional beat: dread blooming inside something familiar.

chapters.title: What Elias Knows
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Elias reveals his mother died in Marrow Creek in 1989, officially a drowning; he's spent thirty years tracing a pattern of 'accidents' tied to the founding families' land deals. He believes the ledger is proof. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose, and a flicker of connection with Juniper.

chapters.title: Ada's Steady Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Juniper visits retired coroner Ada Quill, who taught her everything, and shows her the ledger. Ada's composure cracks for exactly three seconds before she calls it clerical error. Emotional beat: betrayal's first taste; loyalty beginning to fracture.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Juniper cross-references the ledger against property records: seven deaths between 1985 and 1994, each clearing the way for the Hollis-Drayton land consortium. Sheriff Boone Drayton's family name appears twice. Emotional beat: the town she loves becomes a crime scene.

chapters.title: Someone Is Watching
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Elias notices a gray sedan tailing him and finds his motel room searched — nothing taken, everything photographed. Someone wants to know how close he is. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty; the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Exhumation Request
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Juniper files paperwork to exhume one of the ledger's 'accident' victims, forcing Sheriff Drayton to either cooperate or obstruct. He signs it with a smile that doesn't reach his eyes. Emotional beat: quiet defiance; Juniper steps off the sidelines.

chapters.title: The Wrong Coffin
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. The exhumation yields a coffin containing not the expected remains but those of an unidentified man decades younger. Someone swapped bodies. Emotional beat: horror and awe — the conspiracy is more meticulous than imagined.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Elias shares letters his mother wrote before dying, hinting she'd found 'the book of names.' Juniper recognizes the phrasing — it matches marginalia in the ledger. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening between Juniper and Elias over shared obsession.

chapters.title: Threats, Politely Worded
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Anonymous notes arrive at the office suggesting Juniper take early retirement; her cat disappears and returns unharmed — a message, not an accident. Emotional beat: fear met with stubbornness; staying invisible is no longer possible.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Decoding the ledger's margin codes, Juniper finds references to a second volume — the real record — supposedly kept by the original whistleblower, who vanished in 1994. Emotional beat: hope; there may be living proof after all.

chapters.title: Ada Breaks
chapters.summary: POV: Ada (first time). Ada confronts Juniper at night, half-confessing: she falsified records under threat after her husband's death was staged as suicide. She begs Juniper to stop before she's buried too. Emotional beat: tragic complicity; love twisted into silence.

chapters.title: The Centennial Committee
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. The town's centennial gala approaches, chaired by matriarch Vivienne Hollis, who offers Juniper a generous donation to the coroner's office — and mentions Elias's name unprompted. Emotional beat: velvet menace; the enemy wears pearls.

chapters.title: Missing
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Elias goes dark for two days following a lead on the second ledger; Juniper finds his motel room ransacked and blood on the pillowcase. Emotional beat: terror reframed as love — Juniper realizes how much he matters.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Grave
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Using the ledger's date codes, Juniper deduces the vanished whistleblower was buried under a false name in her own cemetery — plot 114, the grave she's tended for years without knowing. Emotional beat: devastating intimacy with the dead; the second ledger may be buried with him.

chapters.title: Unearthing the Truth
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. A midnight dig with her deputy friend Rosa uncovers a sealed tin: the second ledger, photographs, and a confession naming Vivienne Hollis and the elder Drayton. Elias is found alive, held in the Hollis estate's caretaker cottage. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by danger — now they hold everything, and everyone knows it.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Vivienne makes Juniper an offer: full funding, Ada's protection, and Elias freed, in exchange for the tin and silence. Juniper asks for one night to decide. Emotional beat: temptation weighed against duty; love against law made literal.

chapters.title: Staged
chapters.summary: POV: Elias. Elias learns the conspirators plan to kill him and stage it as the 'murder that hasn't happened yet,' framing Juniper for negligence. He escapes the cottage as the trap closes. Emotional beat: race-against-time panic; prophecy turning self-aware.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. At the centennial gala, instead of accepting the offer, Juniper takes the podium and reads the ledger aloud — names, dates, causes of death — while Rosa secures the tin and a state investigator Ada secretly summoned stands ready. Emotional beat: catharsis; the invisible woman making the whole town listen.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Vivienne is arrested; the elder Drayton dies of a stroke before indictment; Sheriff Boone resigns. Ada, confessing fully, faces charges but gains Juniper's guarded forgiveness. Emotional beat: justice outside the law completed by law itself; grief without absolution.

chapters.title: A Name for the Living
chapters.summary: POV: Juniper. Weeks later, Juniper buries the unidentified man from the wrong coffin under his restored true name, with Elias beside her. She files the last of the old secrets, alphabetized, closed. Emotional beat: found family and love chosen freely — Juniper finally belongs to the living.
